Estimate noise dispersion from temporal differences

Source: R/temporal_dispersion.R
temporal_dispersion.Rd

Estimate a pooled marginal noise scale in ordered response channels, allowing for an optional lag-one covariance approximation and a slowly changing mean.

Usage

temporal_dispersion(
  y,
  family = stats::quasipoisson("identity"),
  order = c(2L, 4L, 8L),
  mu = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  rows = NULL,
  minimum_mean = 20,
  method = c("robust", "moment"),
  correlation = c("independent", "lag1"),
  ncores = NULL
)

Arguments

y

Finite ordered observations-by-channels matrix.

family

Scalar GLM family, or one family per channel, supplying the variance function without its dispersion multiplier.

order

Positive difference orders below `nrow(y)`, default `c(2,4,8)`.

mu

Optional independent or smooth pilot means. With `NULL`, Poisson uses raw observations as a linear variance proxy; nonlinear variance functions use a local smooth pilot.

weights

Positive observation precisions, scalar, row vector or matrix. Zero or nonfinite weights exclude difference stencils.

rows

Optional logical eligibility mask, in the same formats as weights.

minimum_mean

Minimum local mean used for relative variance estimates. Gaussian channels use every otherwise eligible stencil.

method

`"robust"` uses squared median absolute differences calibrated to Gaussian noise; `"moment"` uses second moments.

correlation

`"independent"` or `"lag1"`. The latter needs at least two difference orders.

ncores

OpenMP workers; `NULL` uses physical cores.

Value

A list with per-order channel and pooled estimates, summaries `channel` and `pooled`, estimation method and covariance model.

Details

With \(a_k=(-1)^k{r\choose k}\), independent locally stationary noise has \(\operatorname{Var}(\Delta^rY_i)=\phi\sum_k a_k^2V(\mu_{i+k})\). Weighted stencil variances replace \(V(\mu)\) by \(V(\mu)/w\). The native kernel collects valid, locally variance-normalized differences. For locally constant variance and lag-one covariance \(c_1\), $$\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\Delta^rY)}{\sum_k a_k^2} =c_0-\frac{2r}{r+1}c_1.$$ A nonnegative two-endpoint spectral parameterization fits this relationship across orders. The returned `dispersion` is marginal \(c_0\), `lag1` is \(c_1\), and `long_run` is \(c_0+2c_1\). Slowly changing signals are suppressed by high-order differences. Quieter rows or a supplied pilot can reduce contamination from peaks. More extensive serial dependence requires a richer covariance model.

See also

[splogconNMF()]

Examples

set.seed(4)
y <- matrix(rnorm(3000, sd=3), 500, 6)
temporal_dispersion(y, gaussian(), method="moment")$pooled
